source: US Treasury, Treasury International Capital system, annual surveys of foreign holdings of US securities (forms SHL and SHLA, history file shlhistdat.txt): equity plus lt debt by country, $ millions at market value; rows are TIC country codes, total 99996
note: A country is where the bank or broker keeping the securities is based, which is not always where the owner lives, so custody centres such as London, Belgium, Luxembourg and Switzerland hold part of other countries' money. These are the Treasury's yearly surveys, the benchmark its monthly figures are scaled to. They are kept apart from the monthly book, which starts in 2020, because the two agree on totals but not always on the parts. Before June 2002 the surveys covered long-term securities only, and Treasury, agency and corporate bonds are split from December 1994. Not placed with a country is the Treasury's total minus the countries it lists. Old surveys that list some oil exporters only as a group show that group as a row. Dates where the countries fall more than 2.5% short of the total are left out: Dec 1974 (54.6%). Holdings under $500,000 are shown as zero. Source: US Treasury.
